mechanism_narrative: The consistent week-on-week recovery observed in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility at t-0w, coupled with a slight decline in RESIDENTIAL activity, indicates a sustained shift towards out-of-home activities, which will drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing to recover and RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding 10 percentage points as seen at t-0w, acts as a leading indicator for increased weekday foot traffic, directly boosting RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent two weeks following a week where WORKPLACES rose by more than 10 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility, despite remaining elevated, shows a consistent decline for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC simultaneously begins to recover from deep negative values, it signals a cautious but definite return of consumers to public spaces, leading to an increase in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases or stabilizes without further decline, or RETAIL_REC declines again, despite the initial observed pattern.

mechanism_narrative: In a context of easing public health measures, a sustained recovery in TRANSIT station mobility over two consecutive weeks, as observed from t-2w to t-0w, indicates growing public confidence in using shared transport, which directly facilitates greater access to and participation in retail and recreation activities over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility declines again in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite sustained TRANSIT recovery in the specified regime.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent week-on-week recovery in both PARKS and RETAIL_REC mobility at t-0w suggests a general increase in discretionary out-of-home activities, likely driven by improving sentiment or conditions, which will continue to boost retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility declines again in the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite PARKS showing a recovery.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilizes near its baseline (within +/- 5% change) for two consecutive weeks, as seen at t-1w and t-0w, it indicates a normalization of essential shopping patterns, freeing up consumer time and discretionary spending for retail and recreation in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is between -5% and +5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility deviates significantly from the baseline range in the next week, or RETAIL_REC declines in the immediate next week.

mechanism_narrative: A strong inverse relationship where WORKPLACES mobility significantly increases by more than 10 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL mobility simultaneously decreases, indicates a clear and rapid shift away from home-bound activities towards work and associated out-of-home engagements, which will directly translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by >10 points while RESIDENTIAL falls by >1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility declines or RESIDENTIAL mobility increases in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite the observed inverse pattern.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-downturn recovery regime, if a majority of non-residential mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, PARKS, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) show a positive week-on-week change, as observed at t-0w, it signifies a broad-based return to public activity, likely driven by easing policy or public sentiment, leading to increased RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: More than half of the specified non-residential mobility categories decline in the next week, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase despite the initial broad recovery.
